findings.detail: sorted(os.listdir(fd)) materializes all directory names before MAX_ENTRIES and MAX_DEPTH are checked. A large or corrupt journal directory can consume substantial RAM or cause OOM before the intended 256-entry refusal. This contradicts the bounded-RAM operation required for the recovery helper.
findings.hardware_safety_effect: No write-path defect observed; potential diagnostic-process memory exhaustion and failed recovery export.
findings.recommended_fix: Check depth before enumeration; iterate a closable os.scandir(fd), reject when the remaining total entry allowance is exceeded, and only then sort the bounded retained names. Add a regression proving enumeration stops at the first over-limit entry rather than consuming the complete source.
findings.reproduction: A host-only patched enumeration yielded 4096 names with MAX_ENTRIES=256. All 4096 were consumed by sorted before the helper raised its bounds exception.
findings.resolution: Depth is checked before enumeration. A closable os.scandir(fd) iterator increments the shared global count and refuses at MAX_ENTRIES+1 before appending the extra name; sorting occurs only on bounded retained names.
findings.resolution_validation: New lazy 4096-name regression confirms exactly 257 total entries consumed and scanner context closed, both direct and nested. Additional independent probes prove excess depth is refused before child enumeration and a real two-entry parent/child fixture succeeds at allowance 2 but refuses at allowance 1.
findings.title: Directory enumeration allocates unbounded names before enforcing the entry cap

record.followup: No unresolved concrete source defect identified. Coordinator retains integration, live identity checks and hardware acceptance ownership. This source review authorizes no hardware success claim.
reviewed_passes: Fixed NVMe serial/model/bytes, 512-byte logical/physical geometry, exact p1-p5 node set, p4 parent/start/8GiB size and UUID/label match the supplied known-board scope.
SD CID is pinned before both Linux write/discard/flush snapshots; missing or malformed counters fail closed.
Internal journal inode 8 is required and external journal UUID/device are refused. Unknown ext4 incompat features outside the allowed mask are refused; ro,noload suppresses internal replay.

Initial namespace, actual boot pin, RAM root, dedicated tmpfs /run, disabled swap and private root permissions are guarded; RAM root default 1777 normalization is explicitly limited by documentation to a proven RAM boot.
Known NVMe node holders, visible mount namespaces, process FDs/references/maps and swap are checked before the helper opens devices and again after unmount.
libc mount uses read-only,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noload; mounted major/minor, filesystem type, ro protection and noload/norecovery reporting are independently checked.
Held directory FDs plus O_NOFOLLOW confine var/log/journal; cross-device, unsafe owner/mode/type, symlink, hardlink, nonjournal and changed metadata are refused.

File bytes/count/per-file/depth and directory enumeration limits are enforced. Shared entry allowance is checked during scandir before appending, and depth before enumeration; sorting receives at most 256 retained names across the tree. Peak file-byte storage has bounded transient duplication beyond MAX_TOTAL.

Unmount is attempted on collection/verification failure; failed unmount retains mountpoint. Archive output begins only after successful unmount, repeated runtime/identity guards and unchanged SD/NVMe counters.
The docs distinguish host tests, Linux-interval counter equality, raw private data and actual hardware acceptance.
scope_limits: No SSH, mounts, physical-device opens, flashes, commits or source edits performed.
Host mocks and temporary fixtures do not prove board behavior.
Device constants were compared with the coordinator handoff and current implementation status; actual live identity remains a runtime prerequisite.

resolved_defects.description: Mount inventory failure is interpreted as an empty mount inventory. The exit status of lsblk/tr inside the [[ -z $(...) ]] substitution does not control the outer test, so set -e and pipefail do not fail closed.
resolved_defects.evidence: Mock lsblk mount scan exit 1 with empty stdout allowed harmless REACHED_WRITE_STAGE marker and shell exit 0. No dd was invoked.
resolved_defects.recommendation: Capture mount inventory with a standalone assignment whose failure aborts, then test emptiness, e.g. mountpoints=$(lsblk -nr -o MOUNTPOINT "$A733_SD_DEVICE") followed by the existing whitespace-empty check.
resolved_defects.resolution: All type, capacity and mount probes now use standalone assignments under set -e before comparison. Their nonzero status aborts even when stdout would satisfy the comparison.

remaining: Capture requested serial console text; use reviewed RAM recovery only if needed, then collect logs and resolve the actual management fault.
